wg598sj1504.notes: Four figures in ink at the extreme paper edge, no separators, read as 4.4.22. Called medium rather than high because the strokes are thick at this resolution and 1 and 4 share a descender in this hand; if the two opening figures were 1s the reading would be 1.1.22, so the year 1922 holds either way. The printed label on the leader (e4) reads 'WELTE-MIGNON. No. 2621 / Etude Ges dur, Op. 10, No. 5 (Schwarze Tasten) / Fr. Chopin / Gespielt von Tosta di Benici', agreeing with the written number. wj177bx9196.notes: ink on red paper. A flourished cursive name (perhaps Hopf or Kopf, I cannot settle it) followed by a 9 and four plain 1-strokes; separators dropped, and 9 | 11 | 11 is the only split that gives a valid day and month

wj488tq5861.notes: Fine pencil, one line on the upper (upright) panel, no roll number. The month 6 and the year 09 are plain. wk295jd5289.notes: pencil, single line, read from the lower (180-degree) panel; the two year figures are identically formed and read as 2 and 2

wk320bj4724.notes: pencil, separators dropped, read as 10.4.22; crops 1 and 2 hold only ruled pencil lines. The third figure carries an extra top stroke that the two following 2s lack, so read as 4

wn516xn5163.notes: pencil, five digits run together, no separators; grouped 29|6|22. The month figure is a single stroke closing into a bottom bowl, so a 6 rather than the two-stroke 8 of this hand, but it is the one arguable figure

wp442mf3514.notes: Ink, a wide line with the number at the left, the date in the middle and Krämer at the right, Wössler written under Krämer on a second line. wp666fn2104.notes: ink, upright in the lower panel, the same steeply leaning hand as xg976jt9573; read after shearing the line upright. wp877mn0317.notes: crop 1 carries a small two-peak pencil scrawl about 90 px wide, the same in both orientations; it reads as an 'M' or a pair of strokes and holds no figures. Crop 2 shows three ink smudges, not writing. Crops 3 and 4 are perforations only

wq296df7434.notes: Faint ink on paler buff paper, five figures and nothing else. The figures themselves are legible, four cursive 2s of one pattern and a 1, but no points divide them, so the grouping is not fixed by the paper: 21.2.22 or 2.12.22. I give 21.2.22 because the two five-figure inscriptions read so far in this corpus, 14114 and 29125, both take the first two figures as the day; the year is 1922 either way.

ws250sr1272.notes: pencil, five figures run together at the edge of the sheet; read from the lower (180-degree) panel. Figures are plain: a slanted 1, a closed 0 with no descender, a second 1, a 2 with a horizontal base, and a double-bowled 3. Month and year are not in doubt, January 1923. The day is: 10123 could be read 10.1.23 or 1.01.23, and I take the first because this workshop writes a single-figure month unpadded, as in 14114 for 14.1.1914.

ws749sk4778.notes: Ink, one sloping line of five figures with no separators, read 15.8.25 on the corpus convention. The third figure is the 8 of these hands: under threshold it resolves into an upper narrow loop and a lower bowl joined at a crossing node, not the single stroke of a 6. If it were a 6 the month would be June instead.

wt621xq0875.notes: ink, one line, crops 2-4 blank. The figures are legible one by one: 561, then 09, then a final group I read as 04 (a narrow oval joined to a check-mark-and-stem 4). wv641dn9264.notes: All three crops read. Crop 1 shows a faint printed paragraph across the paper, too far gone to read a word of. Not r... tions ab... and placed ... during the ... condi-"), another a torn title slip where only a quotation mark and the figures 06 or 90 survive. Nothing handwritten, no punch date.

wv912mm2332.notes: pencil. Every figure is plain; the grouping follows the corpus convention that 14114 stands for 14.1.1914.

ww627mg3287.notes: ink, a full line across the roll: number, puncher, day, month spelt Novb. and the year in full. Every figure plain

wz252pk3255.inscription: [stamped block of about ten lines of small text, illegible]

wz719qg6993.notes: pencil. Region 1 holds the group 8524 alone, no separators and no name; region 2 carries the roll's number 441 on its own. Read as 8.5.24. The group runs to four figures here where the comparable rolls in this batch have five (ty610zx2946 28622, fr853pn6519 22324, gb034mq5877 11822), which fits a one-figure day and tells against these groups being serial numbers.

xb072rc7617.notes: crop 1 carries a single line of figures near one edge, repeated fainter a little across the paper (an offset, as far as I can see). Selections' and 'is the hole too tight?'; crops 2 and 4 are torn paper with no writing

xc665jf8254.notes: pencil, upper panel upright; a second name stands above Wössler on the same line as the date and I could not read it, roughly seven cursive letters with a u-bow over the penultimate

xg228jc5213.notes: all 3 crops checked, both panels. Crop 1 is the roll end where the red paper meets the green cloth leader, blank apart from a tear; crops 2 and 3 show perforations with a few small ink specks and no figures.

xg670df7262.notes: ink, one line, no number and no name; heavily slanted, read after deslanting. Month is the two-stroke 8 of this hand. The year's first figure is an open arch, so 1 rather than 0, and its second figure has the same closed loop and descender as the 9 of the day

xg924dm1245.notes: Pencil, separators dropped, 13.2.22. The three closing figures are consistent twos.

xg976jt9573.notes: ink, upright in the lower panel, a steeply right-leaning hand; read after shearing the line upright. Six figures, evenly spaced and without separators: 1, 4, 1, 9, 2, 5. The 9 is a closed loop with a plain descender, distinct from the 2 beside it, which carries the usual base stroke. Of the possible groupings only 1 | 4 | 1925 gives a date, so 1 April 1925; 14 | 19 | 25 would need a nineteenth month. The 4 is the least certain figure. Crop 2 carries a pencilled four-figure number, 5571 or 5521, its third figure crossed like a 7; crop 3 shows the printed label, WELTE-MIGNON No. 5521, 'My Isle of Golden Dreams', Waltz, Walter Blaufuss, played by Henry Dark. xh403hj3866.notes: pencil, written across the roll; no roll number or name in the crop

xj540rr2929.notes: Fine pencil, four figures with points between them and nothing else in the crop. Day and month are plain, the 8 showing both loops closed. The two year figures are the same glyph twice, a small top loop over a stroke that falls to the left and curls back at the foot, which I read as the cursive 2 of these hands; read as 9 it would give 1929, outside the range of the corpus. Crops 1 and 2 hold only creases and perforations.

xk500gs5691.notes: Faint pencil. '22' is plain and the last figure is an 8, so 1908 is safe; the middle is either '10' with a single-figure year 8 (22 October 1908) or a month '1' with the year '08' (22 January 1908). I read the marks as '10' then '8' from their spacing, but the other reading is possible. The flourished signature that follows may be Schäfer. Crop 3 shows the leader label 'No. 337 / Berliner Luft / Marsch / P. Lincke / Gespielt von Albrecht Kupfernagel / 4. IV. 05.' — that printed date belongs to the label, not to the punching.

xm418xm6937.notes: roll number only, written in ink across the roll; crop 2 holds a line of small ink specks too small to be writing, crop 3 is plain perforated paper. No date

xm978sg7252.notes: Five pencil figures in e2, written right at the paper edge, with the top of every figure sheared off by that edge even in the extended crop; the lower halves are clear. Read 9 1 8 2 4. The first figure is built exactly like the 9 of the 592 written in e4 (closed oval with the stroke descending to the lower left), not like that hand's 2, which has a flat base to the right. The closing 2 matches the hand's 2; the last figure I take for a 4 from its lower half only. How to group them I cannot settle from the image: 9-18-24 (month first) gives 18 September 1924, while a 2 in place of the 9 would allow 21.8.24 or 2-18-24. The roll is a Welte-Mignon no. 592 with an English label (Brahms waltzes, played by G. Galston, e5), so I cannot assume the German day-first order here. Year 1924 is the part I would stand behind; the day and month I have deliberately left out. e1, e3 blank; e6 colour target.

xm993qd2681.notes: Pencil, one steeply slanted line, read after deshearing and a contrast stretch; the separators are low commas rather than dots. The hand's figures were fixed from within the same line: crop 2 carries the printed leader label 'WELTE-MIGNON No. 1247 Sonata C sharp minor (Moonlight) Part 3, L. v. Beethoven', and the pencil number agrees with it, which gives a 2, a 4 and a 7 to compare against. The day's two figures then match that 2 and 4, the month matches the 2, and the year is the plain 1 of the number followed by the same 4. The 4 and 7 of this hand are close, so the reading rests on that comparison rather than on the figures alone.

xn585zh2707.notes: pencil, four small figures run together, read from the lower (180-degree) panel. A 6 as a large right-opening curve closing into a bottom bowl, then a 7 with its crossbar, then two 2s, each a closed top loop over a stroke that runs down to a long horizontal base. The two 2s are written slightly differently, one loop rounder than the other, and at this resolution the first of them could be taken for a 3, which would make the year 32; the base stroke is what decides it for 2, so 6.7.22.

xn796bh4368.notes: A signature in ink with a long flourish, no date anywhere in the crop. The initial is a looped capital read as C, but G or J would also fit; the surname reads Herrmann. Crops 2 to 4 blank.

xp003dy0437.notes: ink; two names, the first on the date line with two dots set above it (perhaps Krämer), Wössler on a second line below

xq762nt7491.notes: modern felt-tip on the leader, a playing time and the date it was taken, 30 July 2004. Not a punch date. Regions 1, 2, 4, 5 blank.

xr433hz5827.notes: stamped across the roll, upright in the upper panel, smudged and seemingly struck twice. xr682fm1233.notes: fragment of the printed care label on the roll end, no workshop inscription. Region 1 shows show-through only, region 3 is the scanner colour target

III. 07. and the artist's facsimile signature, which I read as beginning H- and ending -yer but cannot fix. xx912rs1788.notes: Ink, one line on the lower (upright) panel, in the order number, date, initials. xy699sy1462.notes: Pencil, five figures on the lower (upright) panel, each plain, with a point after the 6 and none after the 3: 16.3.23. Crop 1 shows only a fine crease running along the paper.

yc867qr9425.notes: all 3 crops checked in both orientations: perforations and a damp stain in 1, blank paper with a scratch in 2, the green cloth leader in 3. No writing

yg667ds7662.notes: Stamped, not written, in a plain sans-serif numeral type; here the UPPER panel is the upright one. zc118hn1152.notes: Pencil, treble edge, five figures without separators. zc614qh7060.notes: pencil, single line, no number or name in the crop; second figure is the open-loop form that can also read as 6, so 26.5.15 is a possible alternative

Chaminade / Played by [facsimile signature]' - printed catalogue label, not a workshop hand, so no roll_number recorded. zf882fv0052.notes: All three crops read. Crop 1 is the cloth leader tab with the scanner's colour target, crop 2 the leader-to-paper join, crop 3 plain red paper with one small dark blemish. No writing in either orientation.

zk440mh1715.notes: pencil, single line, no separators; 23.4.24. Same inscription and hand as hg174cq6672.

zn339mg3395.notes: crop 1 perforations with a faint offset of printed text, crop 2 perforations only, crop 3 the roll end with a printed care label of which only fragments ('…d placed', '…ng the', '…condi-') are legible; no inscription

zp085nr8664.inscription: WELTE-MIGNON No. 3558 SERENADE G. Pierne Played by [signature, illegible]
zp085nr8664.notes: printed box label with the pianist's ink signature, plus the printed care label ('Music-rolls must always be kept in boxes ...'); crop 1 shows that care text stamped or offset onto the roll, far too smudged to read; crop 2 is the spool and colour target. No punch date. The number 3558 is printed on the label, not written on the paper, so roll_number left null

zp424ps8426.notes: printed box label and a printed care slip caught beside the roll end, no workshop hand; crops 1, 3, 4 blank paper and perforations only

zp866tm4852.notes: stamped; the second figure is a 3, its upper bowl open at the left, unlike the closed double bowl of the 8 beside it. A small illegible mark precedes the figures

zr938kz3902.notes: pencil, four figures with no separators, read at the crop turned 180 degrees; on the leader, 9k px into a 454k-px scan, at the treble paper edge. Only the first figure, a 2, is plain; the second and third are taken as 4 and 1 from their shape, and the last could as easily be an 8, which would give 2.4.18 instead of 2.4.13. Crops 1 and 2 hold no writing (crop 2 has a dark blot, not ink strokes).

zt739gs4926.notes: crop 2 carries the number 321, so the four figures on crop 1 are taken as a compressed 4.9.22; same title and same layout as xw872bc8052, which supports the reading, but the grouping is inferred, not written

zv706jf8277.inscription: WELTE-MIGNON No. 458 / Duetto / (Song without Words) A flat major / F. Mendelssohn / Played by [facsimile signature] — beside it the stamp 'Das Recht der Vervielfältigung ... M. WELTE & SÖHNE, G.m.b.H., Freiburg i. B.'
zv706jf8277.notes: printed leader label, not a punch inscription; No. 458 is printed, not written on the paper. Regions 2 and 5 each hold four or five pencil characters at the roll edge, cut off by the edge of the crop and illegible; regions 1, 3, 4, 7 are blank or damp-stained

zv884mc0794.notes: Stamped in black on the bare red paper, the line running diagonally across the roll at about sixty degrees; read after rotating. Five figures with no separators, 2 9 8 2 5, so 29.8.25 on the corpus convention. The third figure is blotted, but thresholding shows two loops each closed on the left, which makes it an 8 and not a 3.

zw485gh6070.notes: Ink, large and unhurried, on clear paper. Third figure of the number is the open-topped 8 of these hands, not a 6; the 8 of the date is a closed figure-eight. A second short signature sits below and right of Roth, four or five cursive letters, which I cannot letter out with any confidence.

zw751nw0097.notes: crop 6 carries a few faint pencil strokes at the roll end beside the green box cloth, three or four cursive characters, too faint and too broken to transcribe; no figures can be made out. Crops 1-5 and 7 blank (scanner lines, creases, a tear, tape). Crop 8 shows the box with a printed English care label, 'Music-rolls must always be placed in Cabinet ... the winter, to prevent ... Not responsible for ...', which is the maker's instruction slip, not a workshop inscription.

zw755dp8285.notes: four cursive digits at the roll edge, read as 5.7.24; not the catalogue number, since the printed leader label in region 3 reads 'WELTE-MIGNON No. 483 / Faust-Walzer / Fr. Liszt / Gespielt von [facsimile signature]'

zw828tx0197.notes: No writing on the paper. The leader label (region 3) reads WELTE-MIGNON No. 3537, Popular Song, Un peu d'amour, L. Silesu, played by (signed) William Daly. Regions 1 and 2 hold only perforations and the cloth leader.

zw904vm6502.notes: All three crops examined. Crop 1 is the scanner's colour target, no paper. Crop 2 has '26. 1. 76' written lengthwise on the grey-green leader tab, all three figure groups plain. As far as I can see this is a later note and not a workshop punch date: it stands on the replacement leader rather than on the red roll paper, and the figure forms differ from the workshop hands in this corpus, so 76 would be 1976, well outside the 1904-1926 range. I have left date_iso null rather than enter it as a punch date. Crop 3 shows printed text bleeding through from the other side of the leader, too faint to recover.

zx463rv8885.notes: ink, two lines, Wössler written under Roth; the umlaut is a bar
